------
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Pradeep Kumar Srivastava
------
For the Petitioner : Mr. Avishek Prasad, Advocate For the State : Mr. Subodh Kr. Dubey, Addl.P.P

------
Order No.07 Dated- 20.04.2023 Heard learned counsel for the parties.

Apprehending his arrest in connection with Argora P.S. Case No. 118 of 2017 corresponding to G.R.
No. 2022 of 2017 instituted under Sections 376, 387, 420, 406, 120-B and 34 of the Indian Penal Code, the petitioner has moved this Court for grant of privilege of anticipatory bail.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner is innocent and has committed no offence at all rather he has been falsely implicated in this case.
It is further submitted that petitioner has never taken money from the informant and all the allegations levelled against him are false and fabricated.
It is further submitted that petitioner has never obtained Aadhar Card or any other document of the informant and never applied for any loan.

It is further submitted that the informant gave money to the petitioner in the year 2006 and the FIR was lodged in the year 2017 for which no reasonable explanation has been offered by the informant for such inordinate delay in lodging this case.
Nothing has been recovered from the possession of petitioner.
Petitioner undertakes to co-operate with the investigation of the case.
Hence, the petitioner may be extended the privilege of anticipatory bail.

Learned Addl.P.P appearing for the State opposes the prayer for anticipatory bail of the petitioner and submits that there is direct and specific allegation against the petitioner that informant is residing at her parental home after some matrimonial discord between the informant and her husband.

Thereafter the informant came into contact with the petitioner and Sapna Choudhary who allured her for providing job in Civil Court in 3rd grade and on this pretext, they cheated Rs.80,000/- from the informant.
It is further contended that petitioner has criminal antecedent and the investigation is at initial stage.

Hence, petitioner may not be extended privilege of anticipatory Yogesh Choudhary @ Yogesh Kumar vs The State Of Jharkhand .... .... ... on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8737775/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It appears that the informant is married lady and she is living separately from her husband at Upper Bazar, Ranchi.
The informant acquainted was with petitioner and Sapna Choudhary.

It further appears that on assurance of providing job in Civil Court, petitioner took Rs.80,000/- from the informant in the presence of witness and also indulged in having physical relationship with her.
Petitioner has also obtained documents like Aadhar Card and other documents and got sanctioned loan in the name of informant by putting her in perplexed situation.
It further appears that the informant has substantiated her version in her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.
From the para 110 of case dairy, it appears that petitioner has criminal antecedent of cheating and N.I. Act cases.

Considering the facts and circumstances as stated above, coupled with materials available on record against the petitioner and in view of criminal background of petitioner, I am not inclined to extend the privilege of anticipatory bail to the petitioner.
Accordingly, the prayer of anticipatory bail application of petitioner is rejected.

(Pradeep Kumar Srivastava, J.) Pappu/
